statement.p: Use the figure below, which gives a graph of the function f(x), to give values for the indicated limits. If a limit does not exist, enter DNE.

image.shortdescription: Graph of a function with some holes and a jump.

description.p: graph of a piecewise defined function, which is an upward opening quadratic function, with vertex at (0,-8), for x in [-3,2]. the function is a line with slope 2 for x greater than 2, starting with an open circle at (2, 2). there is a hole in the line at x=3, and a point plotted at (3, 5).

solution.p: (a) As x approaches -2 from either side, the values of f(x) get closer and closer to -4, so the limit appears to be about -4.

(b) As x approaches 0 from either side, the values of f(x) get closer and closer to -8. (Recall that to find a limit, we are interested in what happens to the function near x but not at x.) The limit appears to be about -8.
(c) As x approaches 2 from either side, the values of f(x) get closer and closer to -4 on one side of x = 2 and get closer and closer to 2 on the other side of x = 2. Thus the limit does not exist.
(d) As x approaches 3 from either side, the values of f(x) get closer and closer to 4. (Again, recall that we don't care what happens right at x = 3.) The limit appears to be about 4.
